title: Spark's cross-instance allocation strategy is an empty placeholder
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.3 is the Allocation Strategy document, and its entire content is: "In the future, additional logic will be added herein regarding the strategy by which capital is allocated between different Instances of the Spark Liquidity Layer."

This is a significant hole given what the surrounding documents claim. The Multi-Instance Coordinator Document exists specifically to "define Spark's overarching strategy and operational framework for managing across all Instances" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2), and the Artifact is otherwise extraordinarily detailed — down to `abi.encodeCall` fragments and per-chain minimum transaction sizes.

What is fully specified is the *envelope*: which venues are permitted, per-instance rate limits, minimum operation sizes, target balances. What is unspecified is the decision function inside it: given yields, risks and limits across a dozen venues, how much goes where. That decision is currently made by the off-chain ALM Planner that holds the Relayer role, following logic no Atlas document states.

So the deployed reality is a governed envelope with a discretionary interior. Constraints are auditable; allocation choices are not. For a mandate whose second half is "deploying collateral backing USDS at attractive risk-adjusted returns," the criteria for what counts as attractive are exactly what the Artifact does not yet contain — making this arguably the single largest documentation gap in Spark's specification.
description: The Allocation Strategy document says only that logic 'will be added herein' in future, so how capital is divided between venues is undocumented while the off-chain ALM Planner already decides it.
